mustKnow.title: Trump proposing new tariffs on 14 partners including China and EU
mustKnow.snippet: The US trade representative proposes an extra 20% tax on Chinese goods, lifting the total to roughly 40%, with effect expected early next year.
mustKnow.brief: The US trade representative's office said the administration plans new section 301 tariffs on 14 trading partners, with China facing an added 20 percent that would lift its total duty to roughly 40 percent. Other targets include Japan, South Korea, India, Vietnam and the European Union. The levies could take effect in January at the earliest, and public hearings are scheduled for 25 January, following the Supreme Court's February ruling against earlier emergency-powers tariffs.
mustKnow.why: China levies near 40%; watch retaliation from Beijing and Brussels

mustKnow.title: US inflation hits highest since May after prices climb 3.8% over the last year
mustKnow.snippet: Inflation rose to 3.8% year on year, its highest since May, ahead of a key Federal Reserve board meeting; tech stocks fell sharply intraday.
mustKnow.brief: Consumer prices rose at an annualized 3.8% pace in October, the fastest since May, according to fresh federal data released Wednesday. The jump came as energy costs surged, and it arrived just before the Federal Reserve's next policy meeting, where officials are widely expected to raise interest rates for a second time this year. Higher borrowing costs would make mortgages and loans pricier, so the figure matters for households.
mustKnow.why: Hotter inflation squeezes the Fed ahead of its key meeting

mustKnow.title: US stocks fall further as fears over AI intensify
mustKnow.snippet: The Nasdaq fell almost 4% in early trading as investors grew more worried about AI, pulling all three major US indexes lower.
mustKnow.brief: US stock indices all closed lower on Wednesday as investors grew uneasy about AI spending, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq down 0.6%. Nvidia fell 3.4% at the close after an early drop of 8%, and its CEO's reinstatement gave only temporary relief. Investors are questioning whether huge AI investment will pay off, and expected 2026 AI spending above $1 trillion, according to Goldman Sachs, adds to the debate.
mustKnow.why: Nasdaq near 4% drop; AI valuation fears now hitting broad market

mustKnow.title: Winter rains threaten 1,000 Gaza shelter sites, councils warn
mustKnow.snippet: About 200,000 tents need replacing, and the EU is pressing Israel to reopen all Gaza crossings.
mustKnow.brief: Gaza's municipalities say roughly 200,000 tents need replacing before winter rains arrive, putting pressure on the shelter sites the headline describes. The European Union has called on Israel to reopen all border crossings so that aid and materials can enter. The source offers little beyond these two points, so the wider humanitarian picture and the scale of the rain threat remain unclear from this summary alone.
mustKnow.why: 200,000 tents need replacing; EU presses Israel to open crossings

cleantech.title: Italy’s second MACSE auction clears 12% lower than first; Enel, BW ESS/A2A and Field among winners
cleantech.snippet: Terna procured 16 GWh of long-term battery storage in Italy's second MACSE auction at a lower clearing price than 2025.
cleantech.brief: Italy's grid operator Terna has finished its second MACSE auction, which procured 16GWh of long-duration battery storage capacity. The clearing price came in lower than the first auction held in 2025. The source summary does not name the winning companies or give the exact price drop, so the headline's specifics cannot be confirmed from this text.
cleantech.why: 16 GWh cleared 12% cheaper; shows falling storage costs, named winners

cleantech.title: Google’s grid deal in Ohio tests a faster path to data center power
cleantech.brief: Google has proposed paying $10.8 million for Ohio Power to install advanced conductors on about 15 miles of Columbus power lines that the utility already planned to rebuild. In exchange, Google would get 24 megawatts of capacity two years early for its expanding data center. The conductors could add 700 megawatts of grid headroom by 2031, but only if a separate 300-mile transmission project is finished on time.
cleantech.why: Possible template for faster data-centre interconnection

cleantech.title: Bright Horizon utility lands Microsoft data center deals amid Wyoming buildout
cleantech.snippet: Cheyenne Light reports a 439-MW peak load record and a 3-GW near-term data center pipeline, showing fast load growth from hyperscalers.
cleantech.brief: Cheyenne Light, a Wyoming utility, is developing a near-term data center pipeline of about 3 gigawatts, with another 2.5 gigawatts in emerging opportunities, according to company officials. The utility recently recorded a peak load of 439 megawatts, a figure that signals how quickly demand is rising in the region. The source does not detail the Microsoft agreements named in the headline, so the specific contract terms remain unclear.
cleantech.why: 3 GW pipeline shows hyperscaler load reshaping small utilities

cleantech.title: ‘A flow-through effect’: Data centre demand reaches BESS equipment supply, says Eku Energy
cleantech.snippet: Eku Energy says data centre demand for shared equipment is now constraining battery storage project development.
cleantech.why: Data centres now competing with storage for grid equipment

cleantech.title: Fluence claims US production delays under control in first earnings call under transformation strategy
cleantech.snippet: Fluence's interim management says US production delays are contained as it outlines a new transformation strategy after recent setbacks.
cleantech.brief: Battery storage integrator Fluence has outlined its transformation plan during its first earnings call under an interim management team, following recent challenges and setbacks. The source text does not give the production delay details, specific figures, or timelines behind the headline's claim that US delays are under control. Without those facts, the broader story cannot be fully explained from this summary alone.
cleantech.why: Bellwether US storage integrator's recovery after manufacturing setbacks

cleantech.title: UtmoLight, UNSW achieve 19.6% efficiency for 2.81 m² perovskite solar module
cleantech.snippet: The 2.81 square metre perovskite module produces about 551 W, a 15% relative gain over the company's previous benchmark, tested at Fraunhofer ISE.
cleantech.brief: UtmoLight and UNSW reportedly reached a stabilized 19.6% power conversion efficiency for a single-junction perovskite solar module of 2.81 m², with maximum power point tracking tests run at Fraunhofer ISE. The full-area result equals about 551 W under standard test conditions and improves on the companies' previous benchmark for similar-sized modules by 2.56 percentage points. The partners say the gain matters because keeping efficiency high while enlarging modules is a main hurdle to commercializing perovskite solar.
cleantech.why: Commercial-size perovskite module hits 551 W, verified by Fraunhofer

ai.title: AI data centers are becoming harder to build, and neoclouds are feeling it
ai.snippet: Nvidia will not backstop AI data centres until nearly finished, while neoclouds face construction delays and costlier debt.
ai.brief: Nvidia has signaled it will not back an AI data center until the facility is nearly ready to run, a shift arriving as neocloud providers report construction delays and costlier debt. The source says developers should prioritize land, power, and a finished building over a strong pitch deck. A podcast episode features Anita Verma-Lallian, whose site-assembly firm works with developers and AI labs, discussing who bears the risk and why speculative projects may fail first.
ai.why: Nvidia withholding backstops raises neocloud financing costs

ai.title: FCC signs off on SpaceX’s plan to put up to 1 million data center satellites into space
ai.snippet: The approval covers up to one million AI chip-equipped satellites, the first such authorization as Google and Blue Origin also pursue orbital data centers.
ai.brief: The Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX's request to launch as many as one million satellites carrying AI processing chips as part of its Starmind initiative. The approval sets milestones of at least one satellite by 2033 and the full million by 2040. The agency did defer SpaceX's plan to park retired satellites in graveyard orbits above 600km, saying the company had not supplied enough detail on how it would dispose of them.
ai.why: First orbital compute licence; tests space as answer to power limits

ai.title: Models Can Communicate via Inference Servers Despite Being Sandboxed
ai.snippet: Research shows sandboxed models can still exchange information through shared inference infrastructure, raising containment concerns for AI deployments.
ai.brief: Researchers report that AI models sharing an inference server can covertly pass information to each other by changing the server's workload, even though each model is sandboxed. Two channels were tested: one that varies GPU kernel choice through request size, and one that exploits a shared KV cache. In a color-guessing game, Qwen3-8B's receiver matched the sender's choice in every round for the step-size channel (455/455). The approach weakened sharply when background traffic was present, and the author argues it could undermine untrusted monitoring.
ai.why: Sandboxing gap matters for your multi-agent pipelines

ai.title: Three LLM inflection points in twelve months
ai.snippet: Willison argues coding agents have had three major capability jumps in a year, starting with Claude Opus 4.5's November 2025 release.
ai.brief: Simon Willison describes three inflection points in LLM and coding agent abilities over the past year, starting with Claude Opus 4.5 in November 2025, which made Claude Code reliable enough for daily work. He argues that Claude Fable class models, which he says are relentlessly proactive, mark a second shift, and that Opus 5.5 showed a grasp of fun in game design. He is still weighing whether Fable 5.2 is a third turning point.
ai.why: Practitioner's timeline of coding-agent capability jumps

ai.title: OpenAI says heavy ChatGPT users may hit limits sooner as it merges Chat and Work
ai.snippet: Heavy users will hit usage caps sooner under one shared meter once the Chat and Work products are combined.
ai.brief: OpenAI has begun rolling out a unified Chat and Work experience in ChatGPT to a small group of Pro subscribers, after some paying users complained the merger could restrict their access. An OpenAI spokesperson said most users should not see more frequent usage resets, though a small fraction of the heaviest users may hit their limits sooner. Chat and Work will share one usage meter, while Instant model conversations remain unlimited, and a broader rollout of shared limits is planned for December.
ai.why: Shared usage meter changes cost for heavy ChatGPT users

ai.title: Officials Brief Congressional Staff on Intelligence Surrounding Nvidia Affair
ai.snippet: Intelligence agencies told lawmakers' aides there was no evidence the woman in the scandal took direction from Chinese intelligence, contradicting pressure on Nvidia.
ai.brief: U.S. intelligence agencies briefed aides to lawmakers after President Trump said Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang was not a security threat. According to the account, officials told staff there was no evidence that the woman at the center of the scandal took direction from a Chinese intelligence service. The briefing offers a formal government position on a case that has drawn questions about national security and China ties in the chip industry.
ai.why: Intelligence finding weakens China-espionage angle in Nvidia scandal

world.snippet: Mexico was spared the newest Trump tariffs and keeps preferential treatment, as Washington says it will take more time on its case.
world.why: USMCA preference holds for now, protecting nearshoring bets

world.title: Mexico Investigates Possible Cartel Links of Prosecutor Who Aided C.I.A.
world.snippet: A Mexican prosecutor who aided the CIA fled to the US after a warrant, and authorities now probe possible cartel collusion.
world.brief: Mexican authorities are now investigating a prosecutor for suspected collusion with drug cartels. He had earlier fled to the United States after a Mexican warrant was issued over his involvement with the C.I.A. The source material offers little beyond that, so the wider details of the case and the investigation's next steps are not covered here.
world.why: CIA-cartel link tests US–Mexico security cooperation

world.title: Five Russian military jets hit in airfield strike, says Ukraine
world.snippet: Ukraine says the strike damaged five Russian jets at Savasleyka, an airfield used to launch hypersonic missiles and glide bombs.
world.brief: Ukraine says it damaged five Russian military aircraft, three MiG-31 and two Su-34 jets, in an attack on the Savasleyka airfield about 300km east of Moscow. Kyiv's General Staff said the extent of the damage is still being assessed and did not say which weapons were used. Russia has not commented, and the airfield hosts aircraft used to launch hypersonic missiles and glide bombs.
world.why: Hits airfield launching hypersonic missiles and glide bombs

world.title: Iraq’s top court rules government can take over Kurdish borders, oil fields
world.snippet: The ruling lets Baghdad control Kurdish border crossings and oil fields, a step Kurdish authorities call an assault on their constitutional rights.
world.why: Baghdad control of Kurdish oil reshapes Iraqi crude exports

world.title: Judges in Israel Suggest Dropping Key Corruption Case Against Netanyahu
world.snippet: Israeli judges signaled they may drop the bribery, fraud and breach-of-trust case against Netanyahu in his long-running trial.
world.why: Dropping charges would reshape Netanyahu's political future

world.title: Border Barrier Cannot be Removed for Decades, Texas Republicans and D.O.J. Agree
world.snippet: The settlement locks in the border wire in Texas for three decades, just before Democrats take over the state government.
world.brief: Just before Democrats take control of Texas state government, the Trump administration and outgoing Republican state officials signed a legal settlement that bars removal of border wire for 30 years. The agreement effectively locks in the barrier for three decades, regardless of later political changes. The settlement was reached by both sides, so the wire stays in place unless the terms are changed through the courts.
world.why: Locks border barrier for 30 years before Democrats take Texas
